source_of_truth: scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/ (plan_review lint module, plan-review CLI, lock + dispatch gates, design-review volley role) plus docs/plans/*/features.json as the artifacts under review

user_journeys.name: plan-review-report
user_journeys.description: As an operator authoring a plan, I run `dontpanic plan-review <plan>` and get a per-feature scope report — size/AC-precision/coupling risk flags with evidence — plus a concrete, conservation-checked split proposal for each over-scoped feature, before I lock or dispatch anything. When the deterministic lint can't fully judge a decomposition, a design-review volley can red-team it.
acceptance_signals: Running plan-review over F007/F012/F008 (onboarding-v0 stalls) flags each with the correct risk class (over-scope / exemplar-AC / silent-prereq).
Each flagged feature yields a split proposal whose child ACs+steps conserve the parent's (no AC dropped or invented).
Surface-count is weighted above AC-count: a 5-AC/3-surface feature flags over-scope while a 4-AC/1-surface feature does not.
A synthetic design-review-volley run (mock executor, no live paid call) yields an oversize finding for a known-oversize decomposition.

user_journeys.name: pre-lock-design-gate
user_journeys.description: As an operator locking a plan, the pre-lock design gate refuses to transition the plan draft->active while any feature carries a block-severity scope flag (over-scope or exemplar/weak acceptance), unless I record an explicit override rationale that lands in decisions.jsonl.
acceptance_signals: Locking an over-scoped plan is refused with a message naming the offending feature and risk class.
Lock succeeds only when the operator supplies an override reason, and that rationale is durably recorded.
A clean plan locks with no override required.

user_journeys.name: mid-dev-scope-delta
user_journeys.description: As an operator editing a locked plan mid-development, the scope-delta check re-lints only the changed features (the diff, not the whole plan), classifies my change as sharpen / expand / split, and enforces the scope-change protocol so drift can't silently re-introduce a stall-causing defect. The same edit-time check flags when a dispatch's diff touches files owned by a DIFFERENT feature (cross-feature bleed).
acceptance_signals: Editing a locked feature to add a second surface is classified `expand` and triggers the scope-change protocol.
Reproducing the F008->F013 cross-feature edit (a patch touching another feature's owned files) is flagged rather than silently accepted.
A purely tightening edit is classified `sharpen` and passes without protocol friction.

user_journeys.name: pre-dispatch-sizing-gate
user_journeys.description: As an operator dispatching a feature, the pre-dispatch sizing gate blocks an over-budget feature before any paid volley round is spent and shows me the split proposal as the remediation, unless I override. This catches scope drift at the exact moment it would otherwise cause a stall.
acceptance_signals: Dispatching an over-budget feature is blocked before the first paid round, with the split proposal surfaced as remediation.
Override is available and recorded when the operator deliberately proceeds.

user_journeys.name: config-readiness-preflight
user_journeys.description: As an operator, when a config file (e.g. quota_caps.json) is invalid or empty, DontPanic stops at pre-flight with an actionable, validated remediation command and a dashboard pointer instead of crashing mid-volley with a low-level schema error. The readiness failure names the specific missing/invalid field and never points back at the command that produced the unready state (no circular remediation).
acceptance_signals: quota_caps.json == {} produces an actionable pre-flight remediation, not a raw schema exception mid-volley (D039).
The remediation names the exact missing/invalid field and is non-circular (does not tell the operator to re-run the command that just produced the unready state, per D002/D003).
Invalid `~/.dontpanic` role strings are surfaced as actionable config-readiness rather than crashing a paid action (D065).

user_journeys.name: close-time-journey-evidence
user_journeys.description: As an operator closing a plan, I can see whether each required journey has captured evidence before the goal-completion audit runs — so journey-evidence is never an afterthought (the D065 lesson). NOTE: this journey is recorded to encode the lesson; its implementation is DEFERRED to a follow-up plan (see pre-impl sufficiency finding) to keep this plan single-surface, mirroring the doctor-WARN deferral in D005.
acceptance_signals: DEFERRED in this plan: no F001-F009 feature implements this; tracked as a follow-up. When built, closing a plan would list each required journey and whether it has captured evidence before the goal-completion audit runs.

required_evidence: Unit tests reproducing each of the three onboarding-v0 stall classes (multi-surface F007, exemplar-AC F008, missing-prereq + weak-test F012) and asserting the matching lint flag fires, with negatives.
Tests proving the pre-lock gate refuses an over-scoped plan and allows it only with a recorded override.
Tests proving the pre-dispatch sizing gate blocks an over-budget feature and surfaces the split proposal.
A synthetic design-review-volley test (mock executor, no live paid call) proving a known-oversize decomposition yields an oversize finding.
Tests reproducing the F008->F013 cross-feature edit and the quota_caps.json == {} hard-stop, asserting the system flags/guides rather than crashes.
non_goals: Replacing the implement->audit volley; this plan reviews plan STRUCTURE, not implementation correctness.
Eliminating all stalls; defects only discoverable by running (e.g. a provider's optimistic status) remain the implement->audit volley's job.
Auto-editing plans without operator approval; split proposals and gates are advisory/override-able, never silent mutations.
Per-plan mandatory paid design-volley; the deterministic lint is the default and the design-volley is triggered only on lint uncertainty or explicit request.

Building the close-time journey-evidence coverage view (journey `close-time-journey-evidence`); the journey is recorded to encode the D065 lesson, but its implementation is deferred to a follow-up plan per the pre-impl sufficiency finding.
completion_test: Running `dontpanic plan-review` over the three onboarding-v0 stall features (F007 pre-split, F008 exemplar-AC, F012 missing-prereq) flags each with the correct risk class and proposes a clean split; the pre-lock and pre-dispatch gates block those features without an override; and the plan-review plan itself passes its own lint (dogfood) with no block-severity flags.
